findings.evidence: Exact rmcp-v3.1.4 ships RequestStateCodec for SEP-2322 requestState. It HMAC-SHA256 seals the state with a domain-separation label, supports associated data and TTL, verifies tags in constant-time, and has exact unit tests for tamper rejection, different-key rejection, associated-data mismatch, missing associated data fail-closed, expiry, and combined TTL/context checks. try_new enforces a 32-byte minimum key.

SealOptions::associated_data is explicitly documented for authenticated principal plus originating-request digest binding; open_with requires the same bytes. This can replace a hand-rolled HMAC layer in the router-first MRTR candidate while preserving method/tool/arguments/principal binding when the server derives canonical associated data.

The exact helper states that single-use/nonce enforcement still has to be implemented server-side. The codec proves integrity/context/TTL, not one-time redemption, task creation idempotency, confidentiality, or effect exactly-once. It is also opt-in rather than an automatic guard on every requestState.

The exact built-in TaskManager is a concrete Clone/Default struct whose only stored state is Arc<Mutex<TaskManagerInner>>, and TaskManagerInner contains a HashMap<String, TaskEntry>. TaskManager::new returns Default. The examined built-in path exposes spawn/get/update/cancel/running_task_count/shutdown rather than a persistent backend injection surface; shutdown drains the map and aborts retained running handles.

TaskManager::spawn always generates uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(), inserts that fresh ID into the in-memory HashMap, then launches the operation with tokio::spawn. The originating JSON-RPC RequestId is captured only for task-local request context propagation, not as the task creation key.

spawn documentation says a task is 'durably observable via get_task before this method returns', but the exact implementation stores the entry only in the manager's in-memory HashMap. Therefore that wording must not be promoted to process-restart durability or persistent create-or-get semantics.

spawn inserts the TaskEntry before constructing/starting tokio::spawn, then stores the JoinHandle afterward; if shutdown drains the entry between launch and handle installation, the returned handle is aborted. This closes that in-process shutdown race, but does not add process-restart recovery because both task state and executor are process memory.

The saved router-first TaskServer candidate can be strengthened by replacing its placeholder request-state verifier with RequestStateCodec::try_new plus seal/open using canonical associated data and TTL. A server-side consumed-op/nonce store is still required if one-time redemption matters. Local cargo remains unavailable, so no compile/runtime success is claimed.

phase1_assessment.reason: The SDK now supplies a strong, tested MRTR requestState integrity primitive and a router-first macro seam, but the built-in TaskManager remains process-memory/fresh-ID execution. RequestStateCodec does not supply server-side one-time redemption, persistent create-or-get, restart redrive, or effect-side exactly-once fencing; a resident persistent backend would remain an unresolved executor dependency.
